info.name: Unified Payment Gateway
info.description:
Try the gateway by hand. Run the folders in order: 1 Health, 2 Admin (create a fake config and grant it), 3 Payments, then 4 PayPal config and 5 Error cases.

Before starting, set the environment variables baseUrl, adminKey, callerKey and clientId (see README.md in this folder).

Folder 8 is the PayPal sandbox scenario step by step: create config, grant, submit payment, open payment_url, get status.

item.name: 8 PayPal sandbox - step by step (tested scenario)
item.description:
The scenario that was run end to end against the PayPal sandbox. Run the requests in order, one at a time.

Before you start: environment variables baseUrl, adminKey (key of an admin client), callerKey (key of a caller client) and clientId (numeric id of that caller) must be set.

1. Create config: put your sandbox client_id / client_secret in the body. return_url points at the gateway itself; {reference} is replaced by the payment id.
2. Grant: lets the caller client use the config.
3. Submit payment: copy payment_url from the response (also written to the Postman Console) and open it in a browser. Log in with a PayPal SANDBOX buyer account and approve.
   PayPal sends the browser back to the gateway return endpoint, which asks PayPal for the real status, captures the order and shows {"status":"paid"}. The URL parameters are never trusted as proof.
4. Get status: confirms PAID (the Webhooks are optional here; they only add a safety net).

Variables written by this folder: ppConfigId, ppCode, ppPaymentUrl. Admin requests use adminKey; payment requests use callerKey (an admin key is rejected on /payments with 403).

request.description: Credentials are stored encrypted and never returned. PayPal accepts USD (not IDR). {reference} in return_url is filled with the payment id when a payment is created. webhook_secret.webhook_id is optional in this scenario.
